audit.whatIsWrong: Teemo's Q is written as "Blinding Shot" in early, wants.you[0], whys[0], whys[1] and whys[3].
audit.why: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json gives slot Q as "Blinding Dart".

audit.whatIsWrong: Renekton's dash is attributed to his W in four places: spikes[1] "his W dash angles", mid "his W landing spot", whys[4] "every W dash angle", wants.you[1] "his W dash landing spots".
audit.why: W is Ruthless Predator — a 300-range point-blank double/triple slash with a stun and no movement at all. The dash is E, Slice and Dice, range 450. Shrooming "W landing spots" is meaningless advice; the mushrooms need to sit where a 450-unit E lands.
audit.corrected: Slice and Dice (E) is the gap-close; place mushrooms on its 450-unit landing spots.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry says "trade around Ruthless Predator's cooldown" everywhere but never states the number, so the player has nothing to count.
audit.why: Ruthless Predator is 16/14/12/10/8s and Slice and Dice is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, while Blinding Dart is a flat 7s at every rank. At rank 1 Teemo gets two full blind cycles for every one stun — that gap is the entire reason a 56% win rate exists in a lane the text describes as losing.
audit.corrected: Ruthless Predator is 16 seconds at rank 1 and your Q is 7 — you get two blinds per stun.

audit.whatIsWrong: The empowered W is repeatedly called "maximum stun duration" / "long stun" without either number.
audit.why: Riot's own text: base Ruthless Predator stuns 0.75s; at 50+ Fury it slashes three times and stuns 1.5s. Double is a very different Move Quick decision from a nudge, and Renekton's Fury bar is visible — it is a readable tell, not a guess.
audit.corrected: Empowered (50+ Fury) stuns 1.5s instead of 0.75s — read the Fury bar before stepping up.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentions anti-heal even though every level-1 and late-game paragraph is about Cull the Meek out-healing Teemo's poison.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags this matchup "needs-antiheal: Renekton sustains through chip damage (Cull the Meek (Q)) — Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades." Cull the Meek is a 7-second AoE that heals off minions as well as champions, so a Teemo who never buys Grievous Wounds is fighting the heal all game. The full layer's Itemization line already says this; the content layer contradicts it by never mentioning it.
audit.corrected: Oblivion Orb before your first completed item — otherwise Cull the Meek refunds the poison every wave.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing flags that Ruthless Predator is an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json: "Renekton's combo opens with an auto-attack reset (Ruthless Predator (W)) — the wind-up is your cue to step back, not the ability cast." The kit carries the autoReset flag on W. The practical consequence for Teemo is that the autos he wants to blind arrive immediately either side of the stun, so the blind has to already be on him, not queued as a reaction.
audit.corrected: W resets his auto timer, so the autos bracket the stun — blind before he closes, not after.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] and whys[5] call the item "Liandry's Anguish"; the full layer's own Itemization line in the same matchup calls it "Liandry's Torment".
audit.why: The two layers cannot both be right. Liandry's Torment is the current name and is what the rest of this dataset uses.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.phases[0].why reads "AA-poke + E poison wins almost every melee level 1" while phases[0].side is "Renekton" at 7/10, and breakdown.early tells the player to respect Ruthless Predator at level 1.
audit.why: Two contradictions in one stage. Renekton is the level-1 winner here precisely because Cull the Meek out-sustains Toxic Shot, which the content layer states correctly. And Ruthless Predator does not exist at level 1 — he has one ability, and it is almost always Cull the Meek.
audit.corrected: Level 1 belongs to Renekton via Cull the Meek's sustain; Ruthless Predator only becomes a threat from level 2.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers publish different level charts for the same matchup, and both are pessimistic for a lane Teemo wins 56.52% of over 683 games. content.win = [Renekton, Skill, Skill, Renekton, Teemo, Skill, Renekton]; full.phases sides = [Renekton, Skill, Teemo, Teemo, Renekton, Teemo, Teemo].
audit.why: They disagree at four of seven stages. content.win[6] = "Renekton" also contradicts this entry's own 'late' paragraph, which argues Teemo wins the 2+ item game on the map and explicitly cites the 56% figure as proof.
audit.corrected: The final stage should read Teemo in both layers, and the two charts should be identical.

audit.whatIsWrong: diff "TRICKY" / diffRating 7.5/10 for a 56.52% matchup with 683 games.
audit.why: 7.5/10 is the rating band this dataset uses for genuinely losing lanes. Renekton's level 1-5 is hard, but the lane resolves in Teemo's favour by a clear margin. No edit proposed: "TRICKY" cannot be swapped for a shorter word inside the length band, and difficulty is partly a how-hard-to-pilot judgement rather than a checkable fact.
audit.corrected: Suggest EVEN / 6.5-7.0 rather than TRICKY / 7.5 — flagged for the user, not edited.

edits.before: Renekton owns level 1 harder than almost any other matchup you face — his Cull the Meek heals back your E poison ticks before they compound, and his base AD means even a Q-blinded auto sequence still gets him minion gold and sustain. Hold your Blinding Shot for the moment he steps up to last-hit, not as a panic button, because he will bait the blind then back off and wait for your cooldown. Levels 2 and 3 are a skill duel: you now have all three abilities, so the moment his empowered Ruthless Predator stun is on cooldown, step up with Toxic Shot and back off immediately with Move Quick — never let him bank two Slice-and-Dice charges to re-engage after your Q lands.
edits.after: Renekton owns level 1 harder than almost any other matchup you face — his Cull the Meek heals back your E poison ticks before they compound, and his base AD means even a Q-blinded auto sequence still gets him minion gold and sustain. Hold your Blinding Dart for the moment he steps up to last-hit, not as a panic button, because he will bait the blind then back off and wait for your cooldown. Levels 2 and 3 are where the numbers start helping you: Ruthless Predator is 16 seconds at rank 1 and Blinding Dart is a flat 7, so you get two blinds for every stun. Step up with Toxic Shot the moment his W goes dark and leave on Move Quick before Slice and Dice is back.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are Renekton's kill window, not yours — he has full fury management, maximum stun duration on the empowered W, and enough base damage to burst you through a blind if Slice-and-Dice brings him close before your Q processes. The plan is survival with profit: push the wave and let him burn his fury on you, heal it back, then watch for his cooldowns going dark. Level 6 flips the script immediately — your first three Noxious Traps go on his W landing spot at the river bush, the tribush approach, and the lane bush. He can no longer dash in without telegraphing through a shroom slow, which cancels his fury dump before the empowered stun can land clean.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are Renekton's kill window, not yours — he has full fury management, the 1.5-second empowered stun, and enough base damage to burst you through a blind if Slice and Dice brings him close before your Q processes. The plan is survival with profit: push the wave, let him spend fury on you, and watch the Fury bar rather than his health bar. Level 6 flips the script immediately — your first three Noxious Traps go where Slice and Dice lands from the river bush, the tribush approach, and the lane bush.
